originality.rationale: Full-text examination of the 2023 open-question paper and the 2024 ordinary-cylinder maximum paper finds neither the complete inclusion-maximal polynomials nor the optimum-slide/jump geometry for the two specific Cartesian prisms. Statement-level comparisons distinguish lower from upper cardinality and ordinary from total visibility. Direct published-finding corpus semantic searches of aliases and asserted numbers identify different graph families and graph properties rather than covering implications. Priority remains provisional, explicitly accounting for an inaccessible plausible older full text and unindexed results.
residual_risks: The complete Cicerone–Di Stefano–Klavžar 2021/2023 paper was not accessible for section-by-section reading; it is a plausible broad-product source.
Unindexed papers, private theses, numerical catalogues or as-yet-unexamined alternate definitions might contain equivalent exact finite tables.
The use of two adjacent finite graphs does not imply any universal odd-even cylinder theorem.

value.rationale: A specifically published open question requests lower mutual visibility on Cartesian cylinders. The two canonical adjacent girth-5 and girth-6 prisms now have complete facet polynomials, explicitly classified minima, and a sharp frozen-vs-connected optimal reconfiguration contrast not implied by their known maximum size. Their precise finite invariants are natural benchmark cases, without pretending to generalize.
